vt29_templars.topic: Templars: founding 1119/1120, Troyes 1129, Omne datum optimum 1139, finance, arrests 13 Oct 1307, Chinon 1308, Vienne 1312, Molay 1314; Friday-13 and Chinon-innocence errors corrected

claims.text: Hugh of Payns and Godfrey of Saint-Omer began the order in 1119 guarding pilgrims on the Jaffa-Jerusalem road; Baldwin II and Patriarch Warmund gave them a base on the Temple platform (al-Aqsa, 'Temple of Solomon'); church sanction probably at Nablus, January 1120; Troyes, January 1129, produced a Latin Rule of 71 clauses; Bernard of Clairvaux wrote In Praise of the New Knighthood
Omne datum optimum, Innocent II, 29 March 1139: privileges to master Robert of Craon; Templars 'defenders of the Catholic Church'; possessions under papal protection

Arrests in France in early hours of Friday 13 October 1307 by Philip IV's officials acting for papal inquisitors; charges: denial of Christ, spitting on the crucifix, indecent kissing, sodomy, idol worship; near-unanimous confessions in Oct-Nov 1307; 'Torture was freely used'; Clement V protested then issued Pastoralis praeeminentiae 22 November 1307 ordering all monarchs to arrest Templars

By early May 1310 almost 600 Templars had agreed to defend the order; 12 May 1310 fifty-four burnt outside Paris as relapsed heretics; Molay and Geoffroi de Charney sentenced 18 March 1314 and burnt that evening on the Ile des Javiaux

Chinon inquiry 17-20 August 1308 by cardinals Berenger Fredol, Etienne de Suisy, Landolfo Brancacci; records confessions, pleas for pardon and absolution from excommunication restoring the leaders to the sacraments; does not declare the Order innocent; Poitiers absolutions 2 July 1308; original D 217, authentic copy D 218; Frale found it September 2001, published J. Medieval History 30 (2004) 109-134; Processus contra Templarios 2007, 799 copies plus one for Benedict XVI; Baluze 1693 published a different Chinon parchment addressed to Philip IV

Vox in excelso, Vienne 22 March 1312, approved 3 April 1312: suppression 'not by definitive sentence, but by apostolic provision or ordinance'; reasons scandal and infamy 'impossible to allay as long as the order continues to exist'; entering or wearing the habit incurs automatic excommunication; more than four-fifths favoured suppression by provision
Ad providam, Vienne 2 May 1312: Templar property granted to the Hospital of St John; property in Castile, Aragon, Portugal and Majorca reserved to the apostolic see

Friday 13 superstition not from the Templar arrests; Lachenmeyer: before 20th c. 'Friday the 13th' not necessarily a concept; 1907 novel Friday, the Thirteenth; Da Vinci Code popularised the Templar link; Holy Blood, Holy Grail 1980s

Templars generated letters of credit for pilgrims who deposited valuables; Philip short of money for war with England; arrests released him from repaying large Templar loans; Philip kept much Templar property in France despite grant to Hospitallers; Order of Christ in Portugal
The Paris Temple soon became 'banker to kings'; the king's treasury accounts kept at the Temple 1221-1295
